sections.heading: How a Vision-Based Position Printing Machine Works
paragraphs: Regular digital printing assumes the fabric is exactly where the file says it should be. Position printing works differently. Position Pro scans the fabric before the print heads fire, reads embroidery, jacquard motifs, lace patterns, pre-printed outlines and panel edges, then matches the artwork to what is actually on the fabric. The vision system corrects offset, skew, rotation, stretch and shrink in real time, so the print lands exactly where it needs to be.

sections.heading: Three Ways Position Printing Adds Value
paragraphs: Print directly over embroidery and textured motifs so colour fills stay inside the intended design. Use position printing for garment panels where logos, borders and engineered patterns need to sit in a precise location. Or print on specialty fabrics such as lace, jacquard, sequined and elastic materials where conventional printing can struggle with alignment.

items.a: Position Pro handles woven fabrics such as cotton, linen, silk, viscose and jacquard, along with knits, lycra, spandex blends, lace, embroidered and sequined fabrics.
Reactive works for cotton, viscose, linen and silk. Acid suits silk, wool and nylon. Pigment works across cotton and blends, while disperse is designed for polyester and polyester blends.

Load the fabric and artwork as a print job. The vision system scans the fabric surface, maps its position and adjusts the artwork before the print heads fire. The machine then prints according to the corrected position.

items.q: What is a position printing machine?
items.a: A position printing machine is a digital textile printer that detects where a design or fabric feature sits and prints exactly on it. It uses vision scanning to align artwork with embroidery, motifs, lace patterns or garment panels, so every print lands in the intended position.

items.q: How is a position printing machine different from a regular digital textile printer?
items.a: A regular digital printer prints the file as-is and assumes the fabric is correctly positioned. A position printing machine scans the fabric first, then corrects for offset, skew and stretch in real time. This makes it suited to pre-embroidered, textured and elastic fabrics where small registration errors can affect the finished piece.

items.q: Which fabrics can Position Pro print on?
items.a: Position Pro handles woven fabrics including cotton, linen, silk, viscose and jacquard, as well as single jersey, interlock, rib, lycra and spandex blends. It also supports lace, embroidered fabric, sequined fabric and double-sided silk printing.

items.q: Can Position Pro print on embroidered or sequined fabric?
items.a: Yes. The vision system maps the embroidery or sequin layout and aligns the print to it, helping colour fills stay within the intended motif instead of shifting beside it.

items.q: What ink types does Position Pro support?
items.a: Position Pro supports reactive, acid, pigment and disperse inks. Reactive is suited to cotton, viscose, linen and silk. Acid is suited to silk, wool and nylon. Pigment works across cotton and blends, while disperse is for polyester and polyester blends.

items.q: What is the production capacity of Position Pro?
items.a: Position Pro runs 16 Kyocera industrial print heads, with a maximum print width of 1,850 mm, resolution up to 1,800 DPI and a 12-colour ink setup.
